title: Chosen One Returns.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only the chosen one will be able [music] to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see black is up a knight and a pawn, but of course everybody can see the fact that we can take this knight with a check. But believe it or not, after this check the material is still equal and there is no checkmate. So this is a draw. But white comes up with the very clever king to F2. And now if black is not careful, this is going to lead [music] to a checkmate in just three moves, so that cannot be allowed. Instead black [music] uses this opportunity to defend the knight with bishop to G2. For the moment black is just up a piece, but white continues with bishop to F3 trying to dislodge the defense of the bishop. Of course the bishop cannot take because of the checkmate we just saw. So instead black plays queen to G7 defending the bishop. Now some of you might notice that white can still take the knight because the bishop is pinned to the king, but actually this leads to a sequence that allows the king to escape. White does win two pieces, but at the end of this sequence the king is going [music] to defend the queen and if a queen trade happens, this is actually a draw. You only have a bishop left. So how can white still make any progress? It seems like everything is defended. Queen to H4 giving a check. This forces knight to H2. Black is simply out of the woods, right? Well, not exactly. White has one of the most incredible moves that I've ever seen. The beautiful, majestic queen to H8. An unbelievable sacrifice that of course cannot be accepted because otherwise bishop takes G2 would be a checkmate. And the sacrifice is on H8 specifically to avoid any checks from the black queen because otherwise we would be able to recapture it. But okay, so what? Black just has to stay on this line, defend the bishop, and there is going to be no way [music] to win for white. But, white is not done. Queen to H7. It's the same exact idea. We are trying to sacrifice the queen to checkmate, and we are covering any potential checks from the black queen. The black queen is running out of squares that it can stay on. It has to go to G5. Queen to H6 follows. The third beautiful sacrifice in a row. Except that queen to [music] H6 stops defending the G8 square, and this allows the black queen to run back and still defend the bishop. What did we achieve? Well, white seems to abandon this idea and plays queen to C1 check. Of course, black has to play knight to F1. But, we already saw this. We saw that this sequence leads to winning the two pieces of black. But, eventually we won't be able to Oh. We were able to move the black queen from G7 to G8. And this one minuscule difference is what allows us now to win the queen and [music] with it the game.
